Amit is the brother of Sonia, Jyoti is the sister of Nikita, Sonia is the daughter of Satish's father. Nikita is the daughter of Kavinder. Jyoti is the mother of Amit, Mukesh is Nikita's only sister's husband. How is Satish related to Kavinder?
solution:
Kavinder's daughters are Jyoti and Nikita. Mukesh is Jyoti's husband. Jyoti is the mother of Amit; Amit, Sonia and Satish are siblings (Sonia is the daughter of Satish's father).

So, Satish is grandson of Kavinder.

stem: In a certain code language, COUNTRY is written as BOWKXLF. How will DESPAIR be written in that language?
solution:
C O U N T R Y $\xrightarrow{+3,-3,+3,-3,+3,-3,+3}$ F L X K W O B; after reversing, BOWKXLF.

Similarly, D E S P A I R $\xrightarrow{+3,-3,+3,-3,+3,-3,+3}$ G B V M D F U; after reversing, UFDMVBG.
notes: Options (A)-(C) are cut off at the right edge of the scan; (A)-(C) partly reconstructed, (D) confirmed by solution.

stem: If the lines $\dfrac{x-2}{1} = \dfrac{y-3}{1} = \dfrac{z-4}{-k}$ and $\dfrac{x-1}{k} = \dfrac{y-4}{2} = \dfrac{z-5}{1}$ are coplanar, then $k$ can have
solution:
Given lines will be coplanar if

$$\begin{vmatrix} -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -k \\ k & 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$$

$\Rightarrow -1(1+2k) - (1+k^2) + 1(2-k) = 0 \Rightarrow k^2 + 3k = 0 \Rightarrow k = 0, -3$

stem: If $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are vectors such that $[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] = 4$, then $[\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\ \ \vec{b}\times\vec{c}\ \ \vec{c}\times\vec{a}] =$
Solution of the differential equation $x\,dy = y\,dx + \sqrt{x^2+y^2}\,dx$ is
solution:
Given equation can be written as $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2+y^2} + y}{x}$ ...(i)

Substituting $y = vx$:

$v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \sqrt{1+v^2} + v \Rightarrow \dfrac{dv}{\sqrt{1+v^2}} = \dfrac{dx}{x}$ ...(ii)

Integrating: $\log(v + \sqrt{1+v^2}) = \log x + \log c$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{y}{x} + \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{y^2}{x^2}} = cx \Rightarrow y + \sqrt{x^2+y^2} = cx^2$

stem: The area included between the parabolas $y^2 = 4a(x+a)$ and $y^2 = 4b(x-a)$, $b > a > 0$, is
solution:
$y^2 = 4a(x+a)$ ...(i) is a parabola with vertex $(-a, 0)$ and $y^2 = 4b(x-a)$ ...(ii) is a parabola with vertex $(a, 0)$.

Solving (i) and (ii), $y = \pm a\sqrt{\dfrac{8b}{b-a}}$

$$A = 2\int_0^{a\sqrt{\frac{8b}{b-a}}}\left[\left(\dfrac{y^2}{4b} + a\right) - \left(\dfrac{y^2}{4a} - a\right)\right]dy = 2\int_0^{a\sqrt{\frac{8b}{b-a}}}\left(2a - \dfrac{(b-a)y^2}{4ab}\right)dy$$

$$= 2\left[2ay - \dfrac{b-a}{12ab}y^3\right]_0^{a\sqrt{\frac{8b}{b-a}}} = \dfrac{8a^2}{3}\sqrt{\dfrac{8b}{b-a}}\ \text{sq. units}$$

$e^{x-[x]} = e^{\{x\}}$ is a periodic function with period $1$.

$= 1000\displaystyle\int_0^1 e^x dx = 1000[e^x]_0^1 = 1000(e-1)$
